clue.text: Daughter had rings put back in ornament

parts.note: two rings look like two letter Os

indicators.note: put back means the word had is turned round to read backwards

explanation.surface: A daughter has returned her rings to a decorative piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodah is an informal word for any small unnamed thing or trinket, such as a decorative knick-knack.

clue.text: Tyler perhaps in Old Norse church keeping lookout

indicators.note: in tells us the rebel's first name sits inside the other letters

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, so Wat is an example of a Tyler

explanation.surface: A Tyler figure keeps watch inside an old Scandinavian church.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler was the leader of the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381; 'perhaps' marks his first name as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on watch is an idiom for being the sentry, keeping a lookout for trouble.

clue.text: Indecisive woman introduces operatic epic

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
The Ring is Wagner's epic four-opera cycle

explanation.surface: A woman introduces someone to a long opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ring (Der Ring des Nibelungen) is Wagner's cycle of four operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithering means wavering, unable to make up one's mind, so it is a synonym of indecisive.

clue.text: Mediocre little house with bad smell

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
a hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A small house with an unpleasant odour is nothing special.
explanation.definitionFit: Ho-hum describes something dull and unremarkable, a synonym of ordinary or middling.

clue.text: Made good or brilliant move in grass

indicators.note: in places the stroke inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a coup is a brilliant, successful stroke

explanation.surface: Someone either succeeded or made a clever play on a lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good a loss is to recover it, a synonym of recouped.

clue.text: Crooked lender accepting current political limit

indicators.note: accepting means the reworked lender letters take in the symbol
crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of lender are rearranged

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A dishonest moneylender takes a cut of the money flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' rearranges LENDER to REDLNE, and 'accepting' takes I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A red line is a boundary in negotiations that one side will not cross.

clue.text: Stock phrases individuals associated with eastern tongue

parts.note: cant is hackneyed, stock talk
individuals are single ones

explanation.surface: Clichéd sayings are linked with a language of the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantonese is a Chinese language, and tongue is a synonym of language.

clue.text: Subject to climatic conditions — suffering from cold?

definitions.meaning: literally exposed to rain, wind and the elements
idiomatically feeling ill, as with a cold

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means slightly unwell, and read literally it means beneath the sky's conditions.

clue.text: Guys risk losing their heads to improve

indicators.note: losing their heads means both words drop their first letters

parts.note: guys are men
to chance something is to risk it

explanation.surface: Men take a gamble by beheading to make things better.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance is to raise in quality, a synonym of make better.

clue.text: Observant lumps about to collar enchantress

indicators.note: to collar means to grab around, so the turned lumps hold the sorceress
about means the word for lumps is turned round

parts.note: nodes are lumps or swellings
a witch is an enchantress

explanation.surface: Lumps somehow wrap themselves round a sorceress, keeping a close eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Lumps here are swellings in medicine, not chunks; 'about' gives SEDON, the turned word, and 'to collar' grips the sorceress in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Switched-on is informal for alert and quick on the uptake, close to observant.

clue.text: Writer's Bloom dropping empty idea

indicators.note: dropping means the flower loses some letters

parts.note: a dahlia is a flower, a bloom

indicators.note: empty means the word idea keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: An author's flower abandons a hollow notion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves I and A from idea, which 'dropping' takes off the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl was a British author, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Burn recusant's nose in scalding vapour

indicators.note: in puts the letter within the vapour

parts.note: steam is scalding vapour

indicators.note: the nose is the front, so take the first letter of recusant's

explanation.surface: A dissenter's nose gets burnt in hot steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' is a Scottish and northern English word for a stream, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a burn is a small river or brook, the same as a stream.

clue.text: Hydrocarbon pioneers modified

indicators.note: modified means the letters of pioneers are changed in order

explanation.surface: Early chemists altered a hydrocarbon.
explanation.definitionFit: Isoprene is a volatile hydrocarbon, the building block of natural rubber.

clue.text: Language teacher has again impressed beginners

indicators.note: beginners means the first letters of the four preceding words

explanation.surface: A language teacher has once more made an impression on novices.
explanation.definitionFit: Thai is the official language of Thailand.

clue.text: See 7
Vigorous number to sing about Romeo

indicators.note: about means the number goes round the letter

parts.note: ten is a number
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: A song number is performed about the romantic lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means forceful and incisive, close to vigorous in argument.

clue.text: Spitfire has course, range and theatre

parts.note: a term is a course of study
an Aga is a make of range cooker
NT is the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: A wartime fighter plane has a flight path, range and theatre of war.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy British range cooker; NT is London's National Theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A spitfire is a fiery, quick-tempered person, a synonym of a shrewish woman.

clue.text: Flower's one in row small child presses

indicators.note: presses means the child squeezes round the disputant

parts.note: a mite is a small child
a row is an argument, so one taking part is an arguer

explanation.surface: A little child presses one of a row of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' here: a quarrel, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The marguerite is a daisy-like flower, the ox-eye daisy.

clue.text: See 20
Clique's member imprisoned at Dartmoor finally

parts.note: inside is slang for in prison

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A gang member is locked up at Dartmoor prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a famous prison in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is one within a closed group, a member of the in-crowd.

clue.text: Fortieth curry for Cockneys

definitions.meaning: a ... wedding is the fortieth anniversary

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang is London slang where a word is replaced by a rhyming phrase, often shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby marks forty years of marriage, and in Cockney rhyming slang a Ruby Murray is a curry.

clue.text: Winds may veer

parts.note: winds that change direction suggest someone changing their mind back and forth

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to vacillate, keep changing one's attitude, as a fickle wind swings round.

clue.text: Strange case in which initially damaged vehicle proceeds

indicators.note: in which means the scrambled case letters hold the other pieces
strange signals the letters of case are scrambled
initially means the first letter of damaged

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An odd case in which a damaged vehicle moves along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' makes ACES from case, and 'in which' puts D and VAN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Advances is a verb meaning moves forward, a synonym of proceeds.

clue.text: Ugly and allowed to go topless

indicators.note: to go topless means losing the first letter

parts.note: lawful means allowed

explanation.surface: Something unsightly and permitted to go bare-chested.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful means very unpleasant, here unsightly.

clue.text: Old sailor wants dosage adjusted

indicators.note: adjusted means the letters of dosage are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly mariner needs his medication changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea dog is an experienced old seaman.

clue.text: Argument against dividing southeast Scots settlement

indicators.note: dividing means the counterargument splits the compass letters

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A dispute splits a Scottish town in the southeast.
explanation.walkthrough: Scone is a village near Perth, Scotland, old crowning place of Scottish kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Scone in Perthshire is a Scottish village, an example of a settlement.

clue.text: Work of genius this is not

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: A modest disclaimer that a piece of writing is no masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work of genius' looks like one phrase, but the definition is 'genius this is not'.
explanation.definitionFit: A goof is a silly blunder, the opposite of a stroke of brilliance.

clue.text: Hectored wife and mother shoved into rotten chore

indicators.note: shoved into means the mother goes inside the scrambled chore letters
rotten means the letters of chore are spoilt and rearranged

parts.note: ma is mother

explanation.surface: A bullied wife and mother is pushed into a nasty household task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' makes ROCHE from chore, and 'shoved into' puts MA inside it. 'Hectored' looks like bullied, but means belonging to Hector.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Andromache was married to Hector, the Trojan hero.

clue.text: Great admirer shows marriage promise subsequently

parts.note: I do is the vow at a wedding
later means subsequently

explanation.surface: A devoted fan shows a wedding vow afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, figuratively a devoted admirer.

clue.text: Possessions in French art gallery

parts.note: ès is French for in, as in docteur ès lettres
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Belongings are kept in a French art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is the whole of a person's property and belongings.
